stem:
Rohit notes that rain still seeps into open ground near his home, yet the neighbourhood tube wells have run lower for several years. More water is pumped out, plant cover has fallen, and a new paved schoolyard covers soil that once soaked up rain.

Why can groundwater decrease even though some water still seeps in?

options.text: Extraction and poorer seepage can remove more groundwater than seepage replaces, so the store falls.
More seepage into the ground always lowers the amount of groundwater available.
Groundwater cannot decrease while the topsoil still looks damp after rain.
Only underground lakes count as groundwater; water in soil pores does not.

teacher.key_rationale: Groundwater is limited. Heavy extraction plus less vegetation and more paving can remove more water than seepage replaces. More seepage does not lower the store; surface dampness and underground lakes alone are not the full story.
